I've been farming these 20 mu for 35 years now, and the wheat-maize rotation is what everyone around here does. Let me think through this year.

For wheat, I planted in October last fall like always. This year I used Jimai 22 again — it's an improved variety, my neighbors and I have gotten good results. On 20 mu of wheat, I put down a compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base, about 50 jin per mu, then topdress with urea at jointing. That works out to around 18 kg N per mu total, 7-8 kg P, and 7-8 kg K. I know from the agro-dealer that wheat needs more nitrogen than phosphorus, and our soil here has decent potassium but I still add some to be safe. Better to spend the extra 30-40 yuan per mu on fertilizer than watch the wheat go yellow.

Irrigation from my well — I'll water 3 times: once before winter (dongshui), once at jointing, once at grain filling. If spring is dry I add one more. For pesticide, I spray herbicide in spring, then once for aphids and powdery mildew around heading. Usually 2-3 sprays total. I plow before planting — rotary tillage. I expect about 450 kg per mu if weather holds.

For summer maize after wheat harvest in June, I go no-till direct seeding — saves time and diesel, and everyone does it now. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or similar — the dealer recommends a newer one but I stick with what I know. I apply about 20 kg N per mu on maize because it's a heavy feeder, split between base and big-trumpet stage. Phosphorus 6 kg, potassium 6 kg. Maize here usually only needs 1 irrigation if summer rain is normal, sometimes 2 if July is dry. Pesticide 2 times — once for corn borer, once for armyworm if they show up. I expect 550 kg per mu.

With 8 people in the household and some working off-farm, I have enough cash for inputs but I'm careful. Not cutting back on fertilizer — a bad harvest hurts more than saving 500 yuan.
